output.summary: The yield decline is real: gauge R&R is stable, the CMM program is unchanged, and tolerances are the same (E4, E2). The new-operator hypothesis is contradicted, since new and experienced operators reject at similar rates and yield fell before any of them ran alone (E14). Several causes remain live and the evidence does not separate them. Hardness spread rose in September lots (E7). Spindle runout exceeds the limit on L3-02 and L3-05, and vibration is rising (E10). Every machine worsened, and the long-shaft machines run tighter tolerances (E11). Fatigue is untested because no hour-of-shift data was collected. The best next step is a staggered spindle service with Tamsworth trial lots and hour-of-machining reconstruction. Reverting shifts, cancelling Corvane, penalizing operators and cutting inspection are premature or harmful.
